metadata.case_name: LAU LI WING v. SECRETARY FOR JUSTICE

injuries.description: mild prolapsed inter vertebral discs at L4/5 and L5/S1 levels
source: An MR1 in September 1995, two years after the accident, showed mild prolapsed inter vertebral discs at L4/5 and L5/S1 levels. It is accepted that these are consequences of the fall. The evidence I accept is conclusive of that.
injuries.icd_description: Certain specified injuries of abdomen, lower back or pelvis

source: She fell on her buttocks and fractured her lower coccyx bone, a type of injury which is known to produce long lasting pain and discomfort even though clinically the fracture unites without apparent problem.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified fracture of lumbar spine or pelvis

injuries.description: some degree of osteoarthritis of the coccyx
source: Dr. David Lee, in his report of 10th November 1995, noted from the X-rays taken by him, that increased density of the coccyx bone demonstrated some degree of osteoarthritis.
injuries.icd_description: Injuries to the abdomen, lower back, lumbar spine or pelvis

source: He describes her state as chronic depression of mood.

manifestations.description: paraesthesia in both lower limbs, especially on the right side
pain at the postero-lateral aspect of both sides of the pelvis
significant reduction in extension of the back and a notable reduction in the flexion on both sides
limited tolerance of sitting, walking and standing
depressed and distressed; anxious about the prospects of finding employment
suicidal (took a drug overdose in July 1995; was in hospital for two days)
reduction in her body weight, in the girth of her lower limbs (lost more than 10 pounds since the accident)

treatments_received: traditional Chinese medicine (external applications and tonic food)
hospital admission (2 days) following drug overdose
treatments_future: psychiatric sessions (recommended by Dr. Chung See-Yuen)

losses.description: Pain suffering and loss of amenity
Virtually unemployable since dismissal on medical grounds; pre-trial and future loss of earnings agreed and awarded
Chronic depression of mood affecting psychological well-being and prospects of employment
Limited tolerance of sitting, walking and standing; reduced extension and flexion of the back
